correctness.rationale: Testing the generator against arbitrary antiderivatives of functions of \(z\) gives the conditional product law. Exact identities for \(L(z^2)\) and \(L(x^2)\) yield the completed-square defect. If equality holds then \(x=0\) on invariant support; compact complete trajectories then force \(z=0\) from \(\dot z=-mz\), followed by \(y=0\). The slab obstruction is the pointwise bound on the completed square inside \([-1/b,0]\). The actual frozen checker was read and its sparse-polynomial certificate was independently inspected.
correctness.risk: The original 2009 full article could not be obtained; one authorized institutional attempt returned an operational error and was not retried.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact attractor-independent height constraint and a sharp recurrence-slab obstruction for a canonical multi-scroll chaotic flow. It converts the defining nonlinear couplings into a structural boundary on every compact recurrent statistical state, not merely a numerical diagnostic.
value.risk: It does not establish existence or ergodicity of a chaotic invariant measure.

final_claim: For the positive-parameter Dadras–Momeni flow, every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=(m/d)z\) and \(\mathbb E[(z+1/(2b))^2]=1/(4b^2)+(ad/(bm))\mathbb E[x^2]\); equality occurs only at the origin, so every other compact stationary state has positive mass in \(\{z<-1/b\}\cup\{z>0\}\).
limitations: Compact invariant measures and periodic orbits only.
The slab theorem forces exit through at least one side but not both for each ergodic component.
